A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central arguments, and retained experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments across random seeds on counting, reverse-order addition, MMLU, and CommonsenseQA, including accuracy and loss distributions.

after.justification: v5 retains original counting, addition, and MMLU results and adds grammatical question-formation experiments, including accuracy distributions, model-depth comparisons, and continuous-loss results.

M1.justification: The distributional analysis, synthetic-task Transformer procedures, and Qwen last-layer/LM-head reinitialization followed by full-parameter training remain unchanged. Question formation extends the experimental application of this framework without introducing a new proposed algorithm or method component.

E1.justification: v5 adds grammatical question formation using synthetic English, ambiguous training examples, and disambiguating out-of-distribution evaluation (Section 4 and Appendix E). It removes CommonsenseQA evaluation from v4 Appendix E.2. Counting, addition, and both Qwen sizes' MMLU coverage remain, including relocated appendix results.

E2.justification: The matched MMLU comparisons retain random guessing and the pretrained Qwen2.5 base-model references. The new question-formation experiments vary data composition and model depth without introducing an evaluated baseline method.

E3.justification: The new question-formation study introduces controlled syntax mixtures, ambiguous versus unambiguous evaluation, and 3- versus 6-layer models trained for 600K steps, evaluated using accuracy and NLL. These constitute a substantial additional experimental design. The retained synthetic and MMLU protocols are unchanged; the CSQA experiments are removed.

E4.justification: v5 adds controlled analyses of whether data composition and model capacity produce consistent hierarchical or linear rules, including persistent failures under entirely hierarchy-inducing data and a continuous-metric check (Figures 6–8). CSQA mixture/scale analyses are removed. The counting inverse-scaling and minimum-depth analyses remain in Appendix C.

E5.justification: v5 adds Hartigan's Dip Test, reporting p < 0.001 for MMLU NLL at the 10% mixture and significance for question-formation NLL without a numerical p-value. Existing seed counts and 95% intervals from 1,000 bootstrap samples remain unchanged; the new study follows the existing 80-seed practice.

E6.justification: v5 adds question-formation accuracy and NLL distributions and depth-comparison findings, while removing CSQA results. Figure 6 reports mean accuracies of 17.2%, 62.5%, 68.8%, and 74.8% at 1%, 10%, 90%, and 100% hierarchical mixtures. Section 4.2 inconsistently describes the 10% mean as 80%. Retained MMLU comparison plots contain the same results.

T1.justification: The maximum-token-loss definition and continuity argument, breakthroughness and linearity formulas, and minimum-probability definition are retained. Equation numbering and presentation change, but no substantive mathematical definition, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the stated empirical scope to grammatical generalization. The central claim that bimodal seed distributions explain apparent breakthroughs remains unchanged. The capacity-threshold argument already existed in v4, and the inverse-scaling claim remains despite its reduced prominence and relocation.

C2.justification: v5 interprets question-formation depth effects as capacity for consistent rule use and tentatively attributes persistent failures to insufficient training-data diversity. It also qualifies retained MMLU findings from consistently outperforming random guessing to performing around or above it. The original distributional and inverse-scaling interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v5 documents question-formation architecture, Adam learning rate and schedule, training duration, grammar-based data construction, and evaluation examples. Existing-task hyperparameters remain. It omits v4's detailed addition index-hint construction description and code/data release promise; no replacement access statement is supplied.

R1.justification: v5 adds targeted grammatical-generalization literature, including Ahuja, McCoy, Mueller and Linzen, and Murty, plus Hartigan's statistical test. It removes the dedicated survey of length-generalization techniques and the CommonsenseQA citation. Positioning against the emergence and mirage accounts remains, with new explicit positioning as extending Qin et al.'s syntax findings.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental explanations, and discussion undergo extensive rewriting and compression. Counting moves into Appendix C, MMLU results subsections are consolidated, and grammatical generalization becomes a main section. The narrative and appendix organization change substantially beyond the addition of scientific content.

P2.justification: v5 adopts two-column main text, redraws summary plots as 2-by-2 grids, combines addition loss and Wasserstein panels, and relocates counting plots. It adds question-formation figures and an examples table, removes the CSQA display, and changes Figure 9 from a density plot to a histogram with a count axis.

improvement.justification: The question-formation experiments add useful evidence about identifiable competing rules in models trained from scratch, while the dip tests strengthen support beyond v4's visual distribution comparisons. These gains modestly improve the central empirical argument. However, v5 removes CSQA validation and the code/data release promise, and its new Section 4.2 reports an 80% mean where Figure 6's corresponding histogram labels 62.5%. These shortcomings limit the overall improvement.
